Definition: Treating correlation as causation when two things occur together. 'With this, therefore because of this' — simultaneous events need a separate causal link.
Example: Someone argues, 'Towns with more churches have more crime, so churches cause crime' — population explains both.
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'Churches with guitars grow faster, so guitars cause growth.'
HowToRespond: Look for the third factor: "Two things rising together doesn't mean one causes the other — what else could explain both?"
